title: the-skills-ask-codemother-who-answers-or-delegates
author: CC (Opus 5), session a187d6ab
owner: codemother owns the face (it is her command surface; ruling 2026-09-06-codemother-owns-the-care-of-the-code); CC builds it; harbor_master keeps the map under delegation; the three SKILL.md edits are tier-2 skill work owned by their charters.
ruling: none — Akien's 2026-09-15 words on idea cdb3e93cdfdd are the spec (recorded verbatim by `cairn review cdb3e93cdfdd`), and his second message the same day: 'harbor_master show map should remain harbor_master's delegated purview. if we asked codemother for the same info, it would still come from the harbor_master anyway. sounds like we have some skills to fix.'
decision_verbatim: i thought we said that code mother answers them all, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY. Harbor master doesn't own the tickets, he just is responsible for tracking them. it's a delegation from one device to another effectively.
pre_approval: none — cast on his words; the build waits its turn in the five-tier order ('fixing chart, sorted, sail and so on sounds next once we wrap the things we've been on', 2026-09-15) and rehearses before BUILDME.
intention: The skills ask codemother for what they need to know about the code — `cairn codemother show artifact <id>` is the first step of /chart, /sorted and /sail — and codemother answers directly or by delegation (the map stays harbor_master's delegated purview, artifacts route to the reader operator_inbox already carries), so `cairn operator` shrinks to what awaits Akien.
why: Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner — codemother owns the care of the code, ruling 2026-09-06-codemother-owns-the-care-of-the-code; a command about the code answered by the operator face has two owners) and Law 1 (a command he could not remember the home of is the resolver spent re-deriving where a settled thing lives).
how: Two arms added to the existing `show` case in cairn/devices/codemother/0/bin/codemother (artifact -> the operator_inbox reader; map -> harbor_master's own show verb, delegated never copied); the three SKILL.md step-0 blocks say `cairn codemother show artifact <id>`; a proof of byte-identity between the codemother and operator verbs over one fixture artifact and of the map arm's exec target; the operator verb's fate and the map breakage's home are open questions on this ticket.
falsifier: RED if, after the build, any of the three skills still names `cairn operator show artifact`; if `cairn codemother show artifact <id>` and `cairn operator show artifact <id>` print different bytes for the same id; if the map verb under codemother does not reach harbor_master's register (a second map is the rival-record failure); or if `cairn operator` gains, rather than loses, a code-facing verb. WRONG-INTENT signal: if the fix copies operator_inbox's reader into codemother instead of delegating — that is the domain box the idea's own author discarded.
traces_to: Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner — codemother owns the care of the code, ruling 2026-09-06-codemother-owns-the-care-of-the-code; a command about the code answered by the operator face has two owners) and Law 1 (a command he could not remember the home of is the resolver spent re-deriving where a settled thing lives).

decisions.text: Codemother answers every command about the code, directly or by delegation; harbor_master tracks tickets under that delegation and never owns them; `cairn operator` is what awaits Akien.
decisions.by: Akien verbatim 2026-09-15 (review of idea cdb3e93cdfdd): 'code mother answers them all, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY. Harbor master doesn't own the tickets, he just is responsible for tracking them. it's a delegation from one device to another effectively.'

decisions.text: `harbor_master show map` stays harbor_master's; codemother's `show map` delegates to it and never copies it.
decisions.by: Akien verbatim 2026-09-15: 'harbor_master show map should remain harbor_master's delegated purview. if we asked codemother for the same info, it would still come from the harbor_master anyway.'

decisions.text: The face ALREADY EXISTS: `cairn codemother` resolves to cairn/devices/codemother/0/bin/codemother (device dispatch through ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/bin), whose `show` verb is a bash case on $what with one arm (dashboard). The build adds two arms, never a new shim: `artifact) exec python3 -m cairn.tools.operator_inbox.inbox show artifact "$@"` and `map) exec "$HOME/.cairn/devices/harbor_master/0/bin/show" map "$@"` (delegation to harbor_master's own show verb, which resolves views through declared_views()); the usage line lists the three.
decisions.by: CC at cast 2026-09-15, CORRECTED the same hour: the first D3 said 'a new bin/cmd/codemother shim' because the census grepped bin/cmd/ and never ran `cairn codemother` — the launcher's device dispatch (bin/cairn:81) already answered. Measured: `cairn codemother show` prints 'usage: cairn codemother show dashboard'.

Not settled here, and therefore a question after cast: whether `cairn operator show artifact` is removed or kept as an alias once the skills stop naming it (he said 'operator becomes about my mail things awaiting me').

challenge_at_birth.better_approach: A symlink `bin/cmd/codemother -> operator` would satisfy the string in the skills with zero code — but it makes codemother's face indistinguishable from the operator's, which is the opposite of the delegation he named (codemother answers, harbor_master tracks, operator is his mail). A dispatch table is the smallest thing that keeps the three faces distinct.
challenge_at_birth.prior_art: In-house: the shim pattern (bin/cmd/question), the reader (cairn.tools.operator_inbox.inbox `show artifact`), harbor_master's register face (`python3 -m cairn.devices.cairn.machines.harbor_master.register`), and the ruling 2026-09-06-codemother-owns-the-care-of-the-code. Memory: recursive-cli-resolution (each segment resolves its children) and inter-device-queries-via-bus-verbs (device A asks device B by a verb) — this is that pattern on the CLI: codemother's segment resolves `show`, and `map` resolves onward to harbor_master.
challenge_at_birth.hidden_assumption: That codemother can have a CLI face before she has a hand (the charter's transitional co-listing names three things she lacks: a hand, a line up, a judgment). A shim that dispatches to existing readers is a face, not a hand — it moves no record, so it does not need the harbor door as actor codemother. If Akien reads a `cairn codemother` verb as implying she acts, that assumption is wrong and the ticket carries a question.
challenge_at_birth.real_collision: None exclusive-and-terminal. The idea's other half ('devices belong to domains and inherit commands') is a distinction the author himself set aside on 2026-09-15 ('the consolidation was the settled half'); recorded, not a collision. Ticket 5ef041fa162a (records carry one extension .artifact) touches the same readers — sequencing, not collision.
